title: Celsus mocks the tree of life
source_text: Οἴεται δὲ καὶ τροπολογοῦντας ἡμᾶς περὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ ἀναπεπλακέναι τὸ ξύλον τῆς ζωῆς καὶ ἀκολούθως ἑαυτοῦ τῷ περὶ τούτου σφάλματί φησιν ὅτι, εἴπερ ἔτυχεν ἐκεῖνος κατὰ κρημνοῦ ἐῤῥιμμένος ἢ (εἰς) βάραθρον ἐωσμένος ἢ ἀγχόνῃ πεπνιγμένος, ἦν ἂν ὑπὲρ τοὺς οὐρανοὺς ἀναπεπλασμένος κρημνὸς ζωῆς ἢ βάραθρον ἀναστάσεως ἢ σχοινίον ἀθανασίας. πάλιν τε αὖ φησιν ὅτι, εἴπερ διὰ τὸ τέκτονα αὐτὸν γεγονέναι ἀναπέπλασται τὸ ξύλον τῆς ζωῆς, ἠκολούθησεν ἂν, εἰ μὲν σκυτοτόμος ἦν, λέγεσθαί τινα περὶ σκύτους ἁγίου, εἰ δὲ λιθοξόος, περὶ λίθου μακαρίου, εἰ δὲ σιδηρεὺς, περὶ σιδήρου ἀγάπης. τίς οὖν οὐχ ὁρᾷ αὐτόθεν τὸ εὐτελὲς αὐτοῦ τῆς κατηγορίας, διαλοιδορουμένου ἀνθρώπους, οὓς ἐπηγγείλατο ἐπιστρέφειν ὡς ἀπατωμένους; ἑξῆς δὲ τούτοις λέγει ἁρμόζοντα μὲν τοῖς ἀναπλάσασι τούς τε λεοντοειδεῖς καὶ ὀνοκεφάλους καὶ δρακοντοειδεῖς ἄρχοντας, καὶ εἴ τις ἐκείνοις παραπλησίως ἐμυθολόγησεν, οὐ μὴν καὶ τοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας. ἀληθῶς γὰρ καὶ γραῦς ἐπὶ τῷ βαυκαλῆσαι παιδίον μεθύουσα μῦθον ἐπᾴδειν τοιοῦτον καὶ ψιθυρίζειν τῷ παιδίῳ ἐπῃσχύνθη, ὁποῖον οἱ τοὺς ὀνοκεφάλους ἀναπλάσαντες καὶ τὰς καθ᾿ ἑκάστην πύλην ὡσπερεὶ δημηγορίας. τὰ δὲ τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας ὁ Κέλσος οὐκ ἐπίσταται, ἅπερ πάνυ ὀλίγοι ἠσκήκασι συνιέναι, οἱ πάντα τὸν βίον ἑαυτῶν ἀναθέντες κατὰ τὴν Ἰησοῦ ἐντολὴν τῷ ἐρευνᾶν „τὰς γραφὰς“ καὶ μᾶλλον τῶν φιλοσοφησάντων Ἑλλήνων περί τινος νομιζομένης ἐπιστήμης ἀνάληψιν κεκμηκότες περὶ τὴν ἐξέτασιν τοῦ βουλήματος τῶν ἱερῶν γραμμάτων.
pass_a_gloss: He supposes (οἴομαι) also us, speaking figuratively (τροπολογέω) about the cross (σταυρός), to have fabricated (ἀναπλάσσω) the tree of life; and consistently (ἀκολούθως) with his own slip (σφάλμα) about this he says that, if that one had happened to be thrown (ῥίπτω) down a cliff (κρημνός) or pushed (ὠθέω) [into] a pit (βάραθρον) or choked (πνίγω) by a noose (ἀγχόνη), there would have been fabricated above the heavens a cliff of life or a pit of resurrection (ἀνάστασις) or a rope (σχοινίον) of immortality (ἀθανασία). And again he says that, if because of his having been a carpenter (τέκτων) the tree of life has been fabricated, it would have followed, if he were a leather-cutter (σκυτοτόμος), that something be said about holy (ἅγιος) leather (σκῦτος); if a stonecutter (λιθοξόος), about a blessed (μακάριος) stone; if a smith (σιδηρεύς), about iron of love (ἀγάπη). Who then does not see straightway (αὐτόθεν) the cheapness (εὐτελές) of his accusation (κατηγορία), as he reviles men whom he professed to turn back (ἐπιστρέφω) as being deceived (ἀπατάω)? Next he says things fitting (ἁρμόζω) those who fabricated the lion-shaped (λεοντοειδής) and ass-headed (ὀνοκέφαλος) and serpent-shaped rulers (ἄρχοντες), and anyone who mythologized (μυθολογέω) like them, but not those from the Church (ἐκκλησία). For truly even an old woman (γραῦς), drunk (μεθύω), to lull (βαυκαλάω) a child, would have been ashamed (ἐπαισχύνομαι) to chant (ἐπᾴδω) such a myth and whisper (ψιθυρίζω) it to the child, as those who fabricated the ass-headed ones and the as-it-were public speeches (δημηγορίαι) at each gate (πύλη). But the [teachings] of those from the Church Celsus does not know (ἐπίσταμαι), which very few have practised (ἀσκέω) to understand (συνίημι): those who have devoted (ἀνατίθημι) all their life, according to the command (ἐντολή) of Jesus, to searching (ἐρευνάω) the Scriptures (γραφαί), and have laboured (κάμνω) about the examination (ἐξέτασις) of the intent (βούλημα) of the sacred writings more than the philosophizing Greeks about the acquisition (ἀνάληψις) of some supposed knowledge.
pass_b_english: He also thinks that we, speaking about the cross in a figurative way, have invented the tree of life (Genesis 2:9). And, in keeping with his own error on this point, he says: “If that man had happened to be flung down a cliff, or pushed into a pit, or choked with a noose, a cliff of life above the heavens would have been invented, or a pit of resurrection, or a rope of immortality.” And again he says: “If the tree of life was invented because he was a carpenter, it would have followed that, had he been a cobbler, something would be said about holy leather; had he been a stonecutter, about a blessed stone; had he been a smith, about an iron of love.”
Who, then, does not see at once how cheap his accusation is, when he heaps abuse on people whom he had undertaken to win back as people who were deceived?

Next after this he says things that fit those who invented the lion-shaped, ass-headed and serpent-shaped rulers, and anyone else who has told myths like theirs, but not those who belong to the Church. For truly, even a drunken old woman singing a child to sleep would have been ashamed to chant and whisper to the child a tale like the one told by those who invented the ass-headed rulers and the speeches, so to speak, made at each gate.

But Celsus does not know the teachings of those who belong to the Church. Very few have trained themselves to understand them: those who, following the command of Jesus, have devoted their whole life to searching “the Scriptures” (John 5:39), and who have toiled over examining the meaning of the sacred writings more than the Greek philosophers toiled to gain some supposed knowledge.

choices.choice: The two conditional sentences after φησιν ὅτι are rendered as Celsus’s own words (ὅτι recitativum; ἐκεῖνος = Jesus). Koetschau supplies (εἰς) before βάραθρον; followed. The sentence ‘For truly, even a drunken old woman...’ is rendered as Origen’s own endorsing remark (ἀληθῶς γάρ), keeping the Greek ambiguity; the TEI does not preserve Koetschau’s spaced type for Celsus fragments, so it may be Celsus’s words that Origen concedes fit the heretics. ‘Rulers’ = ἄρχοντες of the Ophite diagram (see 6.30-31). ‘Speeches at each gate’ = the formulas addressed to the gatekeeping rulers (6.31). John 5:39: ἐρευνᾶτε τὰς γραφάς, taken by Origen as a command. Genesis 2:9 cited at the first mention of the tree of life, which Origen in 6.36 locates in the books of Moses.
'there would have been invented a cliff of life beyond the heavens' -> 'a cliff of life above the heavens would have been invented' (ὑπὲρ τοὺς οὐρανούς; natural order)
'people would speak of some holy leather' -> 'something would be said about holy leather' (λέγεσθαί τινα: passive, τινα is the thing said, not 'some leather')
'whom he professed to turn back as men deceived' -> 'whom he had undertaken to win back as people who were deceived' (ἐπηγγείλατο; dropped stiff 'men deceived')
'such a tale as those have told who invented' -> 'a tale like the one told by those who invented' (stiff Greek order)
checked Genesis 2:9 and John 5:39; Celsus/Origen attribution kept; drunken-old-woman ambiguity already disclosed in notes

choices.choice: 6.37: whether 'For truly, even a drunken old woman...' is a Celsus fragment that Origen endorses or Origen's own remark cannot be settled from the TEI, which lacks Koetschau's spaced type. It stays as Origen's voice, as the Greek frames it (ἀληθῶς γάρ plus the ὁποῖον clause aimed at the heretics), and the existing translator note discloses this. A check against the printed Koetschau page would settle it. Chapter still passed.
